doc.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Yanks and driving a jeep for John Schlesinger
summary: In Yanks with Vanessa Redgrave she plays a Red Cross woman and recalls the nervous jeep scene.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Okay. Creative writing student. When I see that description – Yanks was one of the early ones. It listed you – in 1979 – listed you as the Red Cross lady.

With Vanessa Redgrave. I don’t drive. I can drive, but not in traffic. So I only drive in movies and t.v. There was a scene where Vanessa and I are in a jeep. We have to go down this road, and we suddenly come across a huge area which is showers, and the guys are naked. Just before John Schlesinger, who’s the director, said, “Action,” Vanessa said to me, “I’m told you don’t drive.” I said, “That’s right” – rrrrrrrrr. We did it, and it was fine. Then John said, “We’re going to have to take another angle.” I said, “What?” He said, “Yeah, I want to do a reverse shot,” or whatever. “So will you do it again? I’m going to be – we’re going to build a thing on the front of the jeep on the left-hand side. I’ll be there with a cameraman.” All I could see were headlines: “Famous Director Crushed by a Jeep.” Vanessa was incredible. She was so instinctive. She could go right into a scene.
She was wonderful, and Tony, Tony Richardson.
